original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: In the PR2085/2112 four-target formal register model extended by two nonzero positive rational rank-one added addresses R,S (any direction and scale, possibly coinciding), prove that no exact word of at most seven paid calls uses both R and S, for every finite restored dirty width and free binary mixing.
scope_change_reason: Took the open handoff #6104 question 1 (JoyboyBrian), which is also PR6089's two-frame open question, instead of the card's native larger/nonabelian construction. This is a formal alphabet lower bound on the same endpoint.
bottleneck_link: Scoped side result: adding up to two positive rank-one frames cannot produce a cheaper (fewer than eight call) primitive for this endpoint; such extensions are not a route to a BIT saving here.
stop_rule: Stop at a complete necessary-condition elimination of every count profile with an exact verifier, or at the first surviving profile (reported as the remaining obligation). No word census.
evidence: README.md proof: determinant residual (442 psd profiles), exact support systems (7 free families with old-only supports, 32 pinned splits, all on old directions), exact-lattice character rank kills all pinned splits, uniform 2-local chi_PQ/chi_AB lemma kills the seven free families. verify.py (stdlib, ~5 s) checks all finite steps, 7784 grid regression cases for the free families against both the lemma and the exact lattice a direct-subset-sum regression over 46916 concrete splits of all 442 profiles (648 support survivors, all killed by exact-lattice characters), an eight-call positive control (77 survivors incl. literal word multiplied out) and negative controls.

open_questions.question: Do three or more added positive rank-one frames allow a word of at most seven calls?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Closes the positive-frame extension route for this endpoint at seven calls.
open_questions.first_step: Repeat the support classification with the split replaced by a k-term positive rank-one decomposition of M; check whether free families still force a,b,p,q>=1.
open_questions.blocked_by: 2-local membership of a general multi-term decomposition is not automatic.

open_questions.question: Which eight-call two-frame survivors (for example (1,3,0,1,1,2) with R=2A, S=P/2) are realizable?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Gives the complete two-frame length spectrum, as PR6089 did for one frame; not a cheaper word.
open_questions.first_step: Try subdivision words for each of the 77 eight-call survivors.

open_questions.question: Do indefinite added rank-one frames escape the eight-call floor?
